sentences.text: Callawayia was a small, extinct ichthyosaur that reached a length of 2 to 2.5 meters.
Its skull roof featured large frontals, which are a pair of bones forming the top of the head.
The animal possessed over 54 vertebrae located in front of its hips.
Distinctive double-headed cervical ribs set it apart from the single-headed ribs found behind them.
Its shoulder blades, or scapulae, featured long and narrow shafts.
On each pubic bone, the small opening known as an obturator foramen was not entirely enclosed by bone.
The forelimbs had short, wide humeri with notched front edges.
Callawayia had four digits in its foreflippers and only three digits in its hindflippers.
An additional bone known as a pisiform was present in each foreflipper.
The species name neoscapularis refers to the fact that its shoulder blades resemble those of Jurassic ichthyosaurs more than those of other Triassic ichthyosaurs.
The genus Callawayia was described by Maisch and Matzke in 2000 and named in honor of the ichthyosaur researcher Jack Callaway.

The type species, Callawayia neoscapularis, was originally based on a partial skeleton discovered in 1987 on the shore of Williston Lake in Pink Mountain, British Columbia, Canada, and the holotype specimen was excavated from the "Flipper Quarry" in 1988.
A new species, Callawayia wolonggangense, was named in 2007 based on material found in Guizhou, China.
Callawayia is classified within the family Shastasauridae.
Callawayia lived during the Late Triassic period, specifically the Norian stage between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago, and fossils have been found in what is now Canada.
Nicholls and Manabe considered the naming of Callawayia unethical because the authors were aware that a study naming a different genus was in progress.

In 2016, Ji and colleagues rejected the assignment of Callawayia wolonggangense to the genus Callawayia because they found no characteristics uniting it with the type species, and they also rejected assigning it to the genus Guizhouichthyosaurus due to a lack of unambiguous linking traits.
